Summary

Re-introduce the ability to create a BibEntry by pasting a single textual reference (previously provided by the removed “Import from plain text” feature). This change adds a new “Import from reference text” flow in the UI and plumbing to parse a single reference string into a bibliographic entry using an external reference parsing service.

Motivation

Users often copy single references from PDFs, web pages or other sources and want to quickly add them to JabRef. Re-adding this feature restores that convenient workflow and avoids manual entry for common cases.

What this PR does

- Adds a new dialog/menu action to paste a single reference string and import it as a new entry.
- Introduces an abstraction (ReferenceParserService) for calling external parsing engines and converting their output into JabRef BibEntry objects.
- Implements support for configurable external parsers (initial adapters prepared for Grobid, Cermine and FreeCite — wiring for a default service can be enabled via preferences). The adapters handle invoking the service, parsing the response and mapping fields into a JabRef entry.
- Adds UI preference settings to configure which parser to use and to set endpoint URLs (for self-hosted Grobid/Cermine) or enable public services where applicable.
- Adds basic heuristics/fallback: if the selected external parser fails or returns incomplete data, JabRef will attempt to fallback to a simple rule-based parser to extract common fields (authors, year, title, journal/conference, pages) before presenting a result to the user.
- Adds unit tests for the parser abstraction, adapter mappings and round-trip conversion to BibEntry objects.
- Adds integration tests covering the new dialog and a few representative example reference strings.
- Adds documentation in the import/export settings and the README describing how to enable/use the feature and notes about privacy and running your own parser server.

How it works (user flow)

1. User selects File → Import from reference text (or from the toolbar/context menu).
2. A dialog opens where user pastes a reference string (or multiple lines). Optionally, user can choose which parser to use and which entry type to prefer (article, inproceedings, book, etc.).
3. JabRef sends the string to the configured parser service and receives structured metadata.
4. The dialog shows the parsed fields in an editable preview; user can edit/correct fields before saving.
5. User confirms and the entry is added to the selected library.

Configuration & Privacy

- The feature requires an external parser service. By default, no external calls are made until the user configures a parser endpoint or enables a public service.
- Preferences allow configuring: parser type (Grobid, Cermine, FreeCite, or local rule-based only), service URL, and timeout.
- Documentation warns users that sending reference text to public services may expose bibliographic metadata; instructions for running Grobid/Cermine locally are included.

Limitations & Future work

- Parsing accuracy depends on the chosen service. The adapters include mappings for common output fields, but some fields may need manual correction.
- Initial adapters cover common services; more parsers or improved field mapping rules can be added later (and retraining/fine-tuning is out of scope here).
- The fallback rule-based extractor is intentionally simple; improvements could include using ML-based local parsing or integrating multiple services and voting/merging results.

Testing

- Unit tests added for parsing adapters and mapping logic.
- Integration tests added for the import dialog with a few representative reference strings.

Related

- Original discussion and rationale: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/4717 (removal of the old feature)
- Related prior work: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/2474
- Potential parser projects: Cermine, Grobid, FreeCite
- Research: "Machine Learning vs. Rules and Out-of-the-Box vs. Retrained" (arXiv)

How to test manually

1. Start a supported parser service (e.g., local Grobid or Cermine) or configure a public endpoint in Preferences → Import.
2. Open File → Import from reference text.
3. Paste a reference such as: "Smith, J. and Doe, A. (2018). Example Paper Title. Proceedings of the Example Conf., pp. 12–18." and press Parse.
4. Confirm the parsed preview and save to the library.

Notes for reviewers

- I focused on clean separation between the UI, parsing adapters and mapping logic so we can add more parsers later without touching the UI.
- Please check the field mappings in ParserAdapter* classes for missing fields or inconsistent mapping to BibEntry types.
- Privacy/security implications are documented; feel free to request more explicit warnings in the UI if desired.

  2. Right-click the full-text URL and select Download file.

text:
Summary

Fix a threading/race condition in the autosave system that could cause crashes, hangs, or duplicate concurrent save operations when autosave triggers while another save was in progress or when the app was shutting down.

What I changed

- Introduced a dedicated serial DispatchQueue (AutosaveQueue) for all autosave operations to ensure they never run concurrently.
- Moved autosave scheduling to a DispatchSourceTimer on the serial queue instead of relying on timers that could fire on arbitrary threads.
- Ensured any UI/document state access still happens on the main thread; reads that must be consistent are dispatched to main and results passed back to the serial queue before saving.
- Added an atomic/guard flag (isAutosaveRunning) to prevent reentrant saves and to short-circuit duplicate triggers.
- Properly invalidate and clean up the timer on shutdown/deinit to avoid callbacks after teardown.
- Added unit/integration tests that reproduce the previous race condition and verify the new behavior (single save at a time, no crashes on quit).

Why this fixes the issue

The previous implementation allowed autosave logic to execute from different threads and could start a save while another save was still running. Moving save work to a single serial queue and centralizing scheduling eliminates concurrent execution and prevents races between timer callbacks and teardown.

How to test

- Rapid edit/save: Make frequent changes to a document to trigger autosave repeatedly; verify only one save runs at a time and UI remains responsive.
- App quit during save: Start/trigger an autosave and quit the app; verify there is no crash or deadlock and resources are cleaned up.
- Regression tests: Run the new unit/integration tests included in the PR.

Risk and roll-back plan

- Risk: Low — changes are isolated to the autosave subsystem, and the public save APIs and UI behavior are unchanged.
- Rollback: Revert the autosave threading changes and restore previous timer code if unexpected regressions appear.

Notes

- No data migration needed.
- This also reduces CPU contention by avoiding duplicate save work and makes autosave behavior deterministic.

Summary

This PR prevents JabRef on macOS from forcing the discrete GPU on application start. The problem reoccurred for some users (see original report referencing #4070): on macOS 10.15.3 JabRef would switch to the discrete graphics adapter immediately after launch which is unnecessary and wastes battery.

Why

Setting NSSupportsAutomaticGraphicsSwitching is the recommended way for macOS apps to indicate they do not require the discrete GPU. Previously JabRef's app bundle lacked this hint and macOS could choose the discrete GPU as a precaution.

- Confirmed the Info.plist inside the produced .app contains the new key.

- This change only affects the macOS packaging; no runtime behavior on Windows/Linux changed.
- If you still see graphic switching, please attach a copy of the produced Info.plist and your macOS version so we can investigate further.

Related

- Fixes recurring behaviour originally discussed in #4070.

Summary
This PR fixes a bug where JabRef shows the recovery dialog on startup even though the user had saved and closed the file normally. The problem could be reproduced only after editing a file; files that were opened but not edited did not trigger the dialog.

Root cause
The recovery prompt was triggered whenever a backup (.bak/.sav) file existed for a database opened on startup, without verifying whether the backup actually differed from the saved file on disk. As a result, a stale or newly-created backup could cause an unnecessary recovery dialog even when the last save completed successfully.

What this change does
- Before showing the recovery dialog, the startup logic now compares the current database file to its backup and only prompts if the backup contains different content (i.e. a true divergence indicating unsaved changes or a partial save).
- The backup manager behavior was tightened: on normal close we ensure backup metadata is updated/cleaned so stale backups do not falsely trigger recovery.
- Added unit tests that cover the startup recovery decision logic (cases: edited+saved, edited+unsaved, opened+not-edited).

Why this fixes the issue
By checking whether the backup actually differs from the saved file, we avoid prompting users to recover when their last explicit save completed normally and no real divergence exists between files.

Manual test instructions
1. Delete any .bak/.sav files for a test bib file.
2. Open the test file in JabRef, make edits, save, and close JabRef such that the file is reopened on next start.
3. Start JabRef; before this change the recovery dialog appeared. With this change, no recovery dialog should appear.
4. Verify that when the file has unsaved changes or the backup truly differs, the recovery dialog still appears.

Low-risk change limited to startup recovery logic and backup handling. Unit tests added to prevent regressions.

Rationale
- Previously, the checker inspected the entire title at once and flagged capital letters even when they appeared as the first letter of a subtitle (sentence), which is allowed. Rationale

These changes reduce noise from newline normalization and autosave-induced reloads by preventing unnecessary field writes and undo events. They also avoid the cleanup job from performing redundant newline normalization, which could otherwise produce needless changes.

Summary
Fixes a bug where the text caret would unexpectedly jump to the beginning (line 1, column 1) while typing in large multi-line fields (reported for the "comments" field).

Problem
When the entry text model was refreshed or replaced in response to background updates/listeners, the TextArea/TextField content was replaced wholesale which reset the caret/selection to the start. This was especially visible for long comment fields and frequent background updates.

What I changed
- Preserve caret and selection when updating field content: instead of replacing the whole control text blindly, update only the minimal range or restore the caret/selection after applying changes.
- Debounce/guard model listener updates so UI text is not refreshed unnecessarily while the user is actively editing.
- Use Platform.runLater where necessary to restore caret position after an async UI update to avoid racing with the text control internals.
- Added unit tests and manual test steps that reproduce the previous failure and validate that the caret remains where the user expects.

Fix cursor jumps in entry editor by avoiding unnecessary field updates

Problem:
- While editing multiline fields (e.g. comments) the editor could repeatedly reset the cursor position because the UI layer kept writing back the same value to the entry. This happened due to differences in newline representation between ControlsFX (always '\n') and JabRef (OS-specific newlines) and insignificant whitespace changes.

What I changed:
- AbstractEditorViewModel.bindToEntry():
  - Normalize the existing entry value to ControlsFX newlines (replace OS.NEWLINE with '\n') for comparison.
  - Compare trimmed values using StringUtils.trim(...) and only call entry.setField(...) and push an UndoableFieldChange when the value actually changed. This avoids unnecessary updates and undo edits that caused the editor to reload and reset the caret.
  - Added imports for OS and StringUtils.
- FieldFormatterCleanup.cleanupSingleField():
  - Skip applying NormalizeNewlinesFormatter during cleanup by forcing newValue = oldValue when the formatter is an instance of NormalizeNewlinesFormatter. This prevents cleanup from reporting or performing changes that are only newline normalization differences.

Files modified:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/AbstractEditorViewModel.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/cleanup/FieldFormatterCleanup.java

Why this fixes the issue:
- By performing a normalized, trimmed comparison before writing back to the entry, the editor no longer performs redundant setField calls caused by newline or whitespace representation differences. This stops the periodic reloads that moved the cursor to the beginning.

Summary

This PR refactors and improves how JabRef performs saves, autosaves, and backups. It centralizes save logic, introduces safer atomic file writes, improves autosave scheduling/throttling and UI feedback, and fixes related issues to avoid data loss and redundant disk writes.

Key changes

- Centralized save management: Introduce/extend GlobalSaveManager to become the single place for save operations; SaveAction, SaveAllAction and SaveDatabaseAction now use the centralized API.
- Atomic writes: Add AtomicFileOutputStream and switch file writers (JabRefFileWriter and exporters) to use atomic file output to ensure incomplete writes cannot leave damaged database files.
- Autosave and backup improvements: Refactor AutosaveManager and BackupManager to improve coordination with the centralized save manager and to ensure backups and autosaves are scheduled and executed reliably.
- Autosave throttling: Add DelayTaskThrottler to debounce/throttle frequent save/autosave requests so we avoid excessive disk writes while still persisting data in a timely manner.
- UI integration and events: Add AutosaveEvent and AutosaveUiManager to provide UI feedback about autosave progress and status; JabRefFrame and SharedDatabaseLoginDialogViewModel updated to integrate with autosave/login behaviors.
- Exporter changes: Update TemplateExporter and MSBibExporter to use the new safe file writing approach (through JabRefFileWriter/AtomicFileOutputStream).
- Tests: Update SaveDatabaseActionTest to reflect new save flow and ensure save behavior correctness.
- CLI and startup: Minor adjustments in ArgumentProcessor to align with the new saving/backup/autosave flow.

Motivation

These changes aim to make save operations more robust (preventing partial or corrupted files), reduce unnecessary I/O from frequent saves, and provide better user feedback about autosave/backup operations. Centralizing save logic also reduces duplication and makes future changes easier.

Notes for reviewers

- Focus on the GlobalSaveManager and AtomicFileOutputStream to validate correctness and exception handling for atomic replacements.
- Verify that autosave throttling behavior matches expected timing (DelayTaskThrottler) and that AutosaveEvent notifications are emitted where appropriate.
- Ensure that exporters still produce identical output and that tests cover critical save scenarios.

Summary
Fixes a race condition that could throw an exception when a user-initiated save and an autosave run at the same time.

Problem
When a manual save and the autosave triggered concurrently, both operations could proceed simultaneously and conflict, causing an exception and potentially leaving the document in an inconsistent state.

Fix
Serialize save operations so only one save can run at a time. The change introduces a lightweight synchronization mechanism around the save routine (an async lock/semaphore and an in-flight flag) so autosave checks and either waits for or skips if a save is already running. This guarantees saves do not run concurrently and prevents the exception.

Other changes
- Centralized save logic into a single SaveAsync entry point.
- Added unit/integration tests that simulate concurrent manual and autosave triggers.
- UI: save controls remain responsive and reflect save in progress.

Risk/Compatibility
Low risk: behavior changes only to serialize concurrent save attempts. No data migrations required. Backward-compatible for callers of the public save API.

Testing
Covered by automated tests and manual repro verification: attempted simultaneous manual save + autosave no longer throws and completes successfully.

Introduce a centralized, throttled save implementation and replace low-level file writer usage with a JabRef-aware writer

What changed
- Added JabRefFileWriter: an OutputStreamWriter wrapper that tracks characters that cannot be encoded with the chosen Charset (hasEncodingProblems/getEncodingProblems).
- Added GlobalSaveManager (singleton enum): provides a throttled save API that executes save tasks via DelayTaskThrottler and returns a Future<SaveResult>. SaveResult contains encoding problems and field changes produced by the save.
- Reworked SaveDatabaseAction to use GlobalSaveManager for actual file writes. Saves are scheduled and collected from the returned Future; field changes are registered from the SaveResult and encoding problems are handled by prompting alternative encodings. Updated behavior to handle Interrupted/Execution/Cancellation exceptions gracefully.
- Replaced direct uses of AtomicFileWriter with JabRefFileWriter across exporters (TemplateExporter, MSBibExporter, Autosave/Backup paths, CLI), and removed AtomicFileWriter usage where appropriate.
- Made DelayTaskThrottler generic (DelayTaskThrottler<T>) and adjusted API: new scheduleTask(Callable<T>) that returns ScheduledFuture<T>, with a convenience schedule(Runnable) overload. Internal scheduledFuture type adjusted accordingly and cancel logs debug info.
- Updated places that construct SaveDatabaseAction to pass GlobalSaveManager.INSTANCE (JabRefFrame.confirmClose, AutosaveUiManager, SaveAction, SaveAllAction, SharedDatabaseLoginDialogViewModel, tests). SaveDatabaseAction constructor now requires a GlobalSaveManager parameter.
- AutosaveManager now uses a parameterized DelayTaskThrottler<>. BackupManager and others now use JabRefFileWriter for backups and autosaves.
- Small cleanup: removed trailing blank line in AtomicFileOutputStream and adjusted imports.

Why
- Centralize save behavior to allow throttling/coalescing of frequent save requests (autosave/backups/UI triggered saves) and avoid concurrent or redundant file writes.
- Track encoding issues more robustly via JabRefFileWriter so callers can offer fallback encodings.

Migration notes / API changes
- SaveDatabaseAction constructor signature changed: callers must now supply a GlobalSaveManager (use GlobalSaveManager.INSTANCE).
- DelayTaskThrottler API changed: scheduleTask now expects a Callable and returns ScheduledFuture<T>. There is a new schedule(Runnable) convenience overload. Code using DelayTaskThrottler must adapt to generic typing.
- GlobalSaveManager provides shutdown() to stop the internal throttler if needed.

Tests
- Updated SaveDatabaseActionTest to inject GlobalSaveManager.INSTANCE and adjusted field declarations to final where appropriate.

Potential follow-ups
- Review any other call sites constructing SaveDatabaseAction or using DelayTaskThrottler to ensure they pass the GlobalSaveManager and adapt to the new throttler API.
- Consider additional unit tests around GlobalSaveManager scheduling, encoding-problem reporting, and throttling behavior.

Summary

- Introduce autosave/backup infrastructure and robust save mechanics.

What this PR adds

- Autosave and backup managers
  - AutosaveManager: listens to BibDatabaseContext change events and posts AutosaveEvent via an internal EventBus with throttling to avoid excessive saves.
  - BackupManager: creates periodic backup (.sav) files on changes, can compare, restore and delete backups, and preserves file permissions where possible.
  - AutosaveUiManager: UI-side listener for AutosaveEvent that triggers a silent save of the associated LibraryTab and logs failures.

- Global save and atomic writing
  - GlobalSaveManager: schedules saves via a throttler to avoid concurrent save storms and returns detailed SaveResult (encoding problems + field changes).
  - AtomicFileOutputStream: writes to a temporary file and atomically replaces the target file on close, creating a backup (.bak) and restoring POSIX permissions when possible; supports abort/cleanup and file locking to prevent concurrent writes.
  - JabRefFileWriter: detects characters that cannot be encoded by the chosen Charset and records problematic characters for reporting.

- Save actions and GUI integration
  - SaveDatabaseAction: centralizes save/save-as/save selected logic off the JavaFX thread (BackgroundTask), integrates with AutosaveManager and BackupManager lifecycles, handles encoding problems by offering a choice to try a different encoding, and updates file history and UI state.
  - SaveAction and SaveAllAction: thin GUI wrappers that call SaveDatabaseAction for single/multiple libraries and save variants (save, save as, save selected).
  - Integration in JabRefFrame: when adding a new tab, start AutosaveManager and BackupManager where applicable and register AutosaveUiManager so autosaves produce file writes.

- Export and template exporters
  - TemplateExporter and MSBibExporter updated to use JabRefFileWriter consistently; MSBibExporter forces UTF-8 for XML export to avoid issues with other encodings.
  - TemplateExporter: improved handling of layouts/formatters and blank line behaviour, and loads custom name formatters when present.

- Utilities
  - DelayTaskThrottler: generic throttler used by autosave/backup/global save to coalesce frequent events into a single delayed task.

- Shared DB login improvements
  - SharedDatabaseLoginDialogViewModel: add keystore/SSL support and validation for keystore path; store/recover keystore and server timezone preferences; provide helper dialogs for keystore and save-location selection.

Tests

- SaveDatabaseActionTest: unit tests for SaveDatabaseAction behavior covering:
  - saveAs sets working directory when a path is chosen
  - saveAs does not change working directory when dialog cancelled
  - save falls back to saveAs when database path is absent
  - save retains changed flags on entries
  - save returns false if no path is set

Miscellaneous / Notes

- AutosaveEvent added in model.event to signal autosave operations.
- Several components now rely on the GlobalSaveManager and JabRefFileWriter for consistent reporting of encoding issues and field changes.

Rationale

This change centralizes and stabilizes saving behavior across the application by:
- avoiding excessive save operations via throttling,
- ensuring atomic file writes and backups to reduce risk of data loss,
- surfacing encoding problems to the user and allowing corrective action,
- integrating autosave/backup lifecycle with tab management in the UI,
- adding tests to validate save behavior.

Review guidance

- Pay attention to thread boundaries and use of throttlers/executor shutdown logic.
- Verify that backup/restore and atomic-write semantics behave correctly on POSIX and non-POSIX systems.
- Check user-facing dialogs and messages for save/encoding decisions.
- Ensure SharedDatabaseLoginDialog changes (keystore/SSL) meet security expectations.

text:
Problem summary
- Several users reported saves failing intermittently with filesystem errors (AccessDeniedException on Windows; NoSuchFileException on Linux), likely caused by transient races between writing the temporary .bib.tmp file and moving/renaming it into place (e.g. network drives, LVM caches, antivirus/lockers).
- In addition, autosave and save-related cleanup actions were sometimes running on background threads and mutating JavaFX observable collections / UI elements, triggering frequent exceptions (NullPointerException in ListChangeBuilder and IllegalStateException: Not on FX application thread) and producing hundreds of error dialogs that freeze the UI.

What this PR changes
1. Robust atomic save
   - Improve AtomicFileOutputStream/BibDatabaseWriter to handle transient filesystem move/rename failures:
     - Add a small retry loop with exponential backoff when moving the .tmp file into place, to tolerate transient AccessDeniedException/NoSuchFileException from locks/caches.
     - Ensure temporary files are cleaned up when the move ultimately fails.
   - Log a single, informative error when a save ultimately fails instead of letting the raw exception bubble unhandled.

2. Fix threading and UI-safety for save actions
   - Ensure all modifications to JavaFX ObservableLists / UI properties (tab titles, entry fields updated by cleanup/formatters) are performed on the JavaFX Application Thread via Platform.runLater or by applying changes to a detached model copy before publishing to the UI.
   - Avoid running UI-updating code from autosave background threads; autosave now schedules only the save task on the background thread and delegates any UI updates to the FX thread.

3. Stabilize save-related cleanup
   - Run FieldFormatterCleanups and save-actions in a thread-safe manner: operate on a copy of the BibEntry data or ensure modifications that fire observable events happen on the FX thread to prevent ListChangeBuilder/ObservableList corruption.

4. Autosave behaviour improvements
   - Throttle autosave to prevent overlapping saves: use a single-threaded ScheduledExecutor and ensure a save is not started if a previous save is still running.
   - On repeated failures, show at most one user notification (with details and suggested actions) instead of spawning many modal exception dialogs.

Tests and validation
- Added unit tests covering:
  - Retry behavior for file move under simulated transient failures.
  - That save-related UI updates are executed on the FX thread (using TestFX/Platform.runLater checks).
- Manual testing performed on large databases and on Windows/Linux with simulated locking to verify reduced failure rate and that UI exceptions no longer spam the user.

Why this fixes the reported issues
- The retry/backoff handles transient filesystem races that caused AccessDeniedException and NoSuchFileException when renaming .tmp to the target file.
- Running UI-mutating code on the FX thread (or using model copies) prevents concurrent modifications to JavaFX observable collections, eliminating the ListChangeBuilder and FX-thread IllegalState exceptions.
- Throttling autosave and preventing overlapping saves removes the flood of error dialogs when saves repeatedly fail.

Notes for reviewers
- Key files: org/jabref/logic/exporter/AtomicFileOutputStream.java, org/jabref/logic/exporter/BibDatabaseWriter.java, org/jabref/gui/dialogs/AutosaveUiManager.java, and changes to autosave executor initialization.
- I tried to keep retries conservative (small number of attempts and short exponential backoff) to avoid long blocking saves; open to tuning numbers.
- If desired, we can make retry parameters adjustable via preferences for users on problematic filesystems.

Related reports
- Addresses multiple user reports of save timing problems, filesystem move exceptions, and autosave/FX-thread exceptions observed on Windows and Linux (examples provided in the aggregated issue reports).

text:
Problem: Concurrent saves (user-initiated save + autosave/backup) could race and cause exceptions like AccessDeniedException or NoSuchFileException when the temp file is moved to the target file. Also, autosave invoked saves from non-FX threads which could cause FX thread violations when save actions register UI-related changes.

What this PR does:
- Introduces GlobalSaveManager (singleton) which centralizes saving and serializes/throttles save tasks using DelayTaskThrottler so overlapping saves are queued/cancelled rather than running concurrently.
- Adds JabRefFileWriter to replace AtomicFileWriter for file writes while tracking encoding problems. Save operations now return a SaveResult that includes encoding problems and field-changes produced by save actions.
- Refactors SaveDatabaseAction to use GlobalSaveManager and handle asynchronous save results (Future<SaveResult>), register undoable field changes from the SaveResult, and handle cancellation correctly.
- Makes DelayTaskThrottler generic and adjusts its API (scheduleTask/ schedule/ cancel changes) to support Callable-based throttled tasks and to return typed ScheduledFuture instances. Adds a shutdown method to GlobalSaveManager.
- Replaces usages of AtomicFileWriter with JabRefFileWriter across exporters (MSBibExporter, TemplateExporter, BackupManager, CLI, etc.).
- Updates GUI callers to pass GlobalSaveManager.INSTANCE into SaveDatabaseAction (JabRefFrame, AutosaveUiManager, SaveAction, SaveAllAction, SharedDatabaseLoginDialogViewModel).
- Adjusts AutosaveManager/AutosaveEvent docs and generics to match the throttler changes.
- Fixes minor formatting/cleanup (removed stray trailing newline in AtomicFileOutputStream file) and updates tests to use GlobalSaveManager.

Files changed (high level):
- New: logic/exporter/GlobalSaveManager.java, logic/exporter/JabRefFileWriter.java
- Modified: gui/exporter/SaveDatabaseAction.java and all callers (JabRefFrame, AutosaveUiManager, SaveAction, SaveAllAction, SharedDatabaseLoginDialogViewModel, CLI), logic/util/DelayTaskThrottler.java, logic/autosaveandbackup/*, logic/exporter/* exporters and backup, model event javadoc, tests.

Why this fixes the bug:
- Saves are now throttled/serialized so two concurrent save tasks won't try to move the same temp file at the same time. The actual write is executed off the FX thread and the SaveResult is applied safely, reducing races and FX thread violations.

Notes for reviewers:
- The DelayTaskThrottler API changed (made generic and Callable-based). Reviewers should check call sites and concurrency semantics.
- GlobalSaveManager currently uses a static DelayTaskThrottler and exposes shutdown(); consider lifecycle integration if needed.
- SaveDatabaseAction now depends on GlobalSaveManager; dependency is injected as a singleton instance in callers in this PR. Tests were updated accordingly.

Fix handling of abstract/review fields in LatexFieldFormatter and add tests.

- Bug: LatexFieldFormatter incorrectly computed the doWrap flag using "!isAbstract || !isReview", which evaluates to true for both "abstract" and "review" fields (since a field cannot be both at the same time). As a result, newlines and original formatting in abstract and review fields could be wrapped/altered unexpectedly.

- Fix: Change the logic so wrapping is disabled for either abstract or review fields (doWrap = !(isAbstract || isReview) / !isAbstract && !isReview), preserving their formatting and newlines.

- Tests: Add two unit tests (preserveNewlineInAbstractField and preserveNewlineInReviewField) to assert that newline characters are preserved and the entire field is returned wrapped in the configured value delimiters (i.e. "{...}") for both "abstract" and "review".

- src/test/java/net/sf/jabref/exporter/layout/LatexFieldFormatterTests.java — add tests for abstract and review fields

Summary

This PR fixes several related bugs around line breaks and whitespace handling when editing and writing BibTeX fields:

- Prevent saving of raw line breaks for non-multiline fields (keywords, title, author, etc.).
- Preserve line breaks only for true multiline fields (e.g., abstract, comment) so they render correctly.
- Fix the "Error setting field: bad position" crash that occurred when a non-multiline field contained line breaks and an empty line.

What I changed

- Normalize field values for non-multiline fields before saving/writing:
  - Replace any run of newline characters with a single space.
  - Collapse multiple consecutive whitespace characters to a single space and trim leading/trailing whitespace.
- Ensure multiline fields keep their original newlines and are written unchanged.
- Hardened the field setter to accept input containing empty lines by normalizing it (for non-multiline fields) instead of throwing a position error.
- Added unit tests covering:
  - Saving non-multiline fields with line breaks and empty lines.
  - Confirming multiline fields still preserve line breaks.
  - Regression test that previously reproduced the "bad position" error.
- Updated the BibTeX writer logic to use the normalized values so output files no longer contain unexpected line breaks in single-line fields.

Files touched (high level)

- Field/value setter and validation logic
- BibTeX writer
- Unit tests for field handling and writer
- Changelog entry

Why this fixes the issues

Previously all whitespace and line breaks were preserved for every field, which caused incorrect wrapping of abstract/keyword display and triggered an error when an empty line appeared in a non-multiline field. By treating multiline and non-multiline fields differently and normalizing non-multiline input, we avoid spurious line breaks in the saved database and eliminate the "bad position" error.

Notes

- No visible change to truly multiline fields: abstracts and other intended multi-line content remain the same.
- This PR is backward-compatible for databases that accidentally contained line breaks in single-line fields — those will now be normalized on next save.

References

- Reported issues: "Fix line breaking", "Error setting bibtex field", and "Bibtex writer should not save line breaks for non-multiline fields".

Summary
Implement an alternative merge strategy to safely handle duplicate branch names during merges.

What changed
- Add a new merge implementation that detects duplicate branch names and applies a configurable strategy instead of blindly overwriting.
- Introduce config option duplicateBranchStrategy with supported values: 'keep-first', 'merge-commits', 'rename-with-suffix'. Default preserves existing behavior (keep-first) to remain backward compatible.
- Implement automatic renaming logic that appends a numeric suffix when 'rename-with-suffix' is selected.
- Add unit tests and integration tests covering each strategy and edge cases (conflicting content, identical histories, many duplicates).
- Update documentation and changelog describing the new option and recommended usage.

Why
This prevents accidental overwrites and data loss when multiple branches share the same name across remotes or workflows, and gives teams explicit control over how duplicates are resolved.

Migration / Usage notes
- No behavior change by default.
- To enable the safer behavior, set duplicateBranchStrategy in your config to 'merge-commits' or 'rename-with-suffix'.

Summary

This PR adds an abstract query parsing and mapping layer to convert user-provided queries in a simplified Lucene-like syntax into a structured ComplexSearchQuery that can be forwarded to fetcher APIs. The goal is to let users formulate advanced (fielded) searches in a uniform syntax and allow fetchers to consume structured queries (authors, title phrases, journal, year/year-range, and default terms).

What was added

- QueryParser: Parses a simplified Lucene query string into a ComplexSearchQuery using Lucene's StandardQueryParser. (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/QueryParser.java)
- ComplexSearchQuery: New model + builder representing structured fielded queries (default field phrases, authors, title phrases, journal, single year, year range) with parsing helpers and validation. (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ComplexSearchQuery.java)
- SearchBasedFetcher / SearchBasedParserFetcher: Added/updated default performComplexSearch/getComplexQueryURL behavior and helper to route complex queries to existing performSearch/getURLForQuery when the backend does not support advanced parameters. (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/SearchBasedFetcher.java, SearchBasedParserFetcher.java)
- Fetcher updates: Several fetchers were extended to accept ComplexSearchQuery and to construct API-specific query strings/URLs from it:
  - ArXiv: supports performComplexSearch using field prefixes and ignores unsupported year-range where appropriate. (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ArXiv.java)
  - GoogleScholar: implements performComplexSearch and maps ComplexSearchQuery fields into a Google Scholar query. (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/GoogleScholar.java)
  - IEEE: implements SearchBasedParserFetcher and provides getComplexQueryURL mapping ComplexSearchQuery -> IEEE API parameters. (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/IEEE.java)
  - SpringerFetcher: constructs complex query strings from ComplexSearchQuery for the Springer API. (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/SpringerFetcher.java)
- Tests: Unit tests for query parsing and related behavior were added/updated.
  - QueryParserTest: verifies parsing of default and fielded terms, year and year-range, multiple same-field values. (src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/QueryParserTest.java)
  - ArXivTest: adapted/extended to exercise SearchBasedFetcher capabilities. (src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ArXivTest.java)
- ADR: documentation describing the chosen query syntax and rationale. (docs/adr/0015-support-an-abstract-query-syntax-for-query-conversion.md)
- Module / build updates: project module-info and build.gradle updated to include required Lucene modules/dependencies used by the new parser.

Behavior / Notes

- Supported field names (case-insensitive): author, title, journal, year, year-range, plus unfielded (default) terms.
- Multiple values for the same non-unique fields (e.g. multiple authors/title phrases/default terms) are supported and collected.
- Unique fields (journal, year/single-year/year-range): only a single value is stored; the builder enforces constraints (single year OR year-range). The QueryParser sorts and inserts terms; for unique fields the alphabetically first instance in the query string is used (see QueryParser javadoc).
- Default implementations ensure backward compatibility: if a fetcher does not override performComplexSearch/getComplexQueryURL, the complex query will be converted to default field phrases and routed to performSearch/getURLForQuery.
- Quoting: ComplexSearchQuery builder strips/normalizes quotes and wraps values in quotes where appropriate so fetchers receive consistent phrases.

Why

This change standardizes how advanced, fielded searches are expressed by users and enables fetchers to use more precise API parameters where available. Using a Lucene-derived syntax reduces learning curve and enables reuse of tested parsing code.

- Run unit tests (especially QueryParserTest and fetcher tests).
- Spot-check fetcher behavior for complex queries (author:, ti:, journal:, year:, year-range:) and verify results are consistent with previous behavior when only simple queries are used.
- Review the ADR for the intended syntax and limitations.

- Added/changed: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ComplexSearchQuery.java

text:
Fix module access error in chipview (entry editor) when running from Eclipse

Problem
- Running JabRef from Eclipse caused an IllegalAccessError in the chip view of the entry editor:
  java.lang.IllegalAccessError: class com.jfoenix.controls.JFXAutoCompletePopup (in module com.jfoenix) cannot access class com.sun.javafx.stage.PopupWindowHelper (in module javafx.graphics) because module javafx.graphics does not export com.sun.javafx.stage to module com.jfoenix
- This was introduced by the change in #6228 and is triggered by the Java module system blocking access to internal JavaFX classes used by JFoenix.

Cause
- JFoenix's JFXAutoCompletePopup relies on an internal JavaFX class (com.sun.javafx.stage.PopupWindowHelper) that is not exported by the javafx.graphics module, so the reflective access fails under the module system (Java 9+), in particular when running inside IDEs like Eclipse.

What I changed
- Removed the dependency on the internal com.sun.javafx.stage API used by the autocomplete popup in the chip view.
- Replaced usage of JFXAutoCompletePopup with an implementation that uses supported, public JavaFX APIs (PopupControl/Popup or a small wrapper) to present the autocomplete popup. This avoids reflective access to internal packages and works correctly under the Java module system.
- Updated the chip view to use the new popup implementation while preserving existing behavior and styling.
- Added a unit/integration test that verifies the autocomplete popup opens and closes correctly when running in a modular environment.
- Added a note to the developer README explaining the previous module access problem and how to run the application from the IDE if developers still need to use older native JFoenix features (alternate workaround using --add-exports is documented for devs only).

Verification
- Tested running JabRef from Eclipse and confirmed the IllegalAccessError no longer occurs and the chip/autocomplete behavior is unchanged.
- Also verified the packaged application (non-modular run) still works as before.

Notes
- This is a behavior-preserving fix that removes reliance on JavaFX internal APIs and resolves the runtime error introduced in #6228.

Fixes: #6228

text:
Fix startup crash on Windows XP caused by unconditional native binding of a Windows 7+ API

Problem
- On Windows XP JabRef-2.11b5 fails to start with an UnsatisfiedLinkError: Error looking up function 'SetCurrentProcessExplicitAppUserModelID'. The exception happens during static initialization of the WindowsExtensions native binding (JNA tries to register a function that does not exist on XP), which aborts startup and prevents any UI from appearing.

Root cause
- WindowsExtensions registered the native function SetCurrentProcessExplicitAppUserModelID unconditionally. That API is only available on newer Windows versions (Windows 7+). On XP the function is not present, causing JNA to throw UnsatisfiedLinkError during class initialization and crash the application.

What this change does
- Makes loading of the AppUserModelID native function optional and fail-safe:
  - Move native registration out of an unconditional static initializer and into a guarded initialization block.
  - Detect missing native function or registration failures (catch UnsatisfiedLinkError / Throwable) and disable AppUserModelID-related functionality when the function cannot be loaded.
  - Add logging so failure to load the native function is recorded, but does not abort startup.

Behavioral notes
- On Windows XP (or other environments where SetCurrentProcessExplicitAppUserModelID is unavailable) JabRef will now start normally; features that depend on AppUserModelID will be gracefully disabled.
- On Windows 7+ the native function will load and AppUserModelID functionality continues to work unchanged.
- No functional changes are made for non-Windows platforms.

Files changed (high level)
- net/sf/jabref/gui/nativeext/WindowsExtensions.java
  - Replace unconditional Native.register usage with guarded, lazy initialization and exception handling.
- Logging added to report inability to register the native function.

Testing / How to reproduce
- Before fix: run "java -jar JabRef-2.11b5.jar" on a Windows XP VM with Java 1.7.0_04 — app fails to start and shows UnsatisfiedLinkError for SetCurrentProcessExplicitAppUserModelID.
- After fix: same command should start JabRef normally on XP (no windowless crash). On Windows 7+ verify AppUserModelID-related behavior still works.

Follow-ups
- Consider consolidating native bindings and runtime capability probing in a small helper to make future additions of optional native calls simpler and less error-prone.
- Add an automated integration test (if possible) that verifies startup on older Windows versions or simulates missing native symbols.

What changed
- DOIResolutionFetcher: after resolving the DOI to a URL, check the host against the fetcher registry. If a tailored fetcher exists for that host, return nothing/empty instead of returning a fetch result.

Summary
Fix the Snapcraft build failure in CI by adding the required parse-info metadata to the 'jabref' part so that 'adopt-info' can operate correctly.

Background
CI was failing with the error: "Failed to generate snap metadata: 'adopt-info' refers to part 'jabref', but that part is lacking the 'parse-info' property." This happens because adopt-info expects the part it adopts metadata from to define how to parse upstream archive info.

What I changed
- Added a parse-info block to the jabref part in snap/snapcraft.yaml so Snapcraft can extract metadata (name/version/files) from the downloaded JabRef portable tarball.
- Ensured the adopt-info entry references the jabref part (unchanged) and can now pick up the parsed metadata.
- Included a brief comment explaining why parse-info is required, and how it maps to the downloaded archive.

Why this fixes the problem
adopt-info requires the source part to expose parsing instructions (parse-info) so it can read upstream package metadata. Providing parse-info for the jabref part satisfies this requirement and prevents the metadata generation failure seen in the workflow.

Validation
- This change targets the snapcraft.yaml only; CI snap build should no longer fail with the parse-info error.
- To test locally: run snapcraft pack (or snapcraft --debug) for the snap build step and verify metadata generation completes.

References
- CI failure: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/runs/1262693776?check_suite_focus=true
- Related discussion: https://forum.snapcraft.io/t/failed-to-generate-snap-metadata-adopt-info-refers-to-part-synfig-studio-but-that-part-is-lacking-the-parse-info-property/18733/11

Notes for reviewers
Please check the parse-info pattern matches the downloaded archive name and that no additional packaging changes are required for the snap pipeline. If acceptable, merge to restore the Snap build in CI.

Summary:
This pull request fixes import/export failures for PostgreSQL reported in the issue where operations failed with the errors "This connection has been closed" (export) and "This ResultSet is closed." (import). The problem was caused by premature closing of JDBC resources during the import/export workflow which is incompatible with the PostgreSQL JDBC driver's expectations.

What I changed:
- Reworked resource management for SQL import/export flows so Connections, Statements and ResultSets remain open for the duration of the operation and are closed only after all data processing is complete.
- Replaced manual try/finally cleanup with scoped try-with-resources (where appropriate) and ensured the close order is safe for all supported drivers.
- Moved connection close logic out of intermediate helper methods so a connection is not closed while a ResultSet or Statement is still in use.

- Added an integration test that runs import and export against a local PostgreSQL instance (can be skipped if DB not available) and unit tests that assert resources are closed only after processing.

Why this fixes the issue:
PostgreSQL's JDBC driver disallows using a ResultSet or Statement after the Connection/Statement has been closed. The previous code closed resources too early in certain execution paths, which led to the observed exceptions. The new resource management ensures we process all rows before closing JDBC objects.

Testing performed:
- Manual verification of import and export using PostgreSQL 9.x/10.x with the dataset that previously triggered the error.
- Unit tests asserting correct order of close operations.
- Ran existing test-suite to ensure no regressions in other database backends.

- No changes to public APIs.
- Behavior is unchanged for other database backends; this is a safer resource-management approach and should reduce similar errors across drivers.
- If you run the integration test locally, ensure a PostgreSQL instance is available and the test DB credentials are configured.

Fixes: the reported import/export failures for PostgreSQL (issue: "Import/Export to external database fails for PostgreSQL in 3.0 of jabref").

text:
Summary

This PR improves parsing, representation and lookup of linked file values used in .bib file fields. It makes FileFieldParser and LinkedFile more robust when handling escaped characters, XML entities, malformed URLs and platform-specific paths, and adds/updates unit tests to cover these scenarios.

Changes

- FileFieldParser
  - Robust parsing of file field strings: properly handles escaped characters (\\, :, ;) and XML character sequences such as , so semicolons inside XML entities are ignored when splitting.
  - Accepts and preserves malformed URL-like strings when the scheme is escaped (e.g. "https\://...") so they can still be stored as links.
  - Treats strings that contain "//" as likely malformed URLs (keeps them as raw path strings) instead of attempting to interpret them as valid paths.
  - Ensures the converter side-effect is documented and that the input list is cleared after conversion (existing behavior retained).

- LinkedFile
  - Normalizes local path separators by replacing backslashes with forward slashes when setting a non-online link.
  - Uses Path.of(...) to validate paths and to create a NULL_OBJECT; catches InvalidPathException so invalid paths are stored as raw strings (preserving user data).
  - findIn(...) now uses Path.of and returns Optional.empty() for invalid paths.
  - Online link detection remains based on http(s) prefix or presence of "www.".
  - Serialization (writeObject/readObject) of transient JavaFX properties is preserved.

- Tests
  - FileFieldParserTest: covers a wide range of cases including null/empty inputs, escaped separators, XML characters, online URLs (valid and malformed), Windows paths, missing fields, multiple entries and too many separators.
  - FileFieldWriterTest: verifies quoting/encoding and string representation for Windows-style paths.

Why

These changes fix multiple edge cases when reading/writing the special file field format used by JabRef, especially for Windows paths, escaped characters and imperfect/malformed URLs encountered in real-world .bib files. By validating paths with Path.of and catching InvalidPathException, the code avoids exceptions and preserves data when paths are invalid.

Summary

Fix the Harvard/RTF export so that "and" inside brace-protected names is no longer treated as a name separator. The export previously split name fields on every occurrence of "and" without respecting BibTeX braced groups, which caused entries like { {Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development} } or { {Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development and other stuff} } to be broken and recombined incorrectly.

Why this fixes the issue

Previously the exporter treated every literal "and" as separating distinct names; it ignored the BibTeX convention where double curly braces (or balanced braces) protect an entire name as a single unit. By honoring brace-delimited groups when splitting, the exporter now preserves organization names and other braced names exactly as intended.

Summary
Fixed an issue where secondary sorting (tie-breaker sort) was ignored for certain special field types, causing results to be ordered incorrectly when the primary sort produced equal values.

Problem
- Secondary sort key was not applied for some special fields such as multi-valued fields, scripted/computed fields, and fields with missing or non-primitive representations.
- Root cause: the comparator/normalization step did not handle these special cases (multi-valued, null/missing, or computed values) and sometimes returned values that could not be compared consistently. In addition, there was no reliable tie-breaker fallback when values compared as equal.

What I changed
- Normalize values used for sorting for the affected field types so they become comparable across documents (handle multi-valued fields by defining a consistent pick strategy, normalize null/missing values, and evaluate scripted/computed fields before comparison).
- Add a robust tie-breaker fallback (document id) to guarantee a stable secondary order when both primary and secondary keys are equal after normalization.
- Ensure the comparator is stable and handles edge cases without throwing for uncommon field representations.

Tests
- Added unit tests and integration tests covering:
  - Multi-valued fields
  - Scripted/computed fields
  - Fields with missing/null values
  - Cases where primary sort produces ties and secondary sort must be applied
- Existing tests updated where necessary to reflect deterministic ordering.

Compatibility and performance
- No schema or data migrations required.
- Normalization introduces minimal overhead; benchmarks show no significant regression on typical workloads.

Summary

Make the BibTeX parser tolerant of input where entries are not separated by a newline. Previously the parser could fail or merge entries when a closing brace (}) for one entry was immediately followed by the @ of the next entry on the same line.

- Improve tokenization/state transitions so that entries are recognized correctly even when there is no separating newline or when only whitespace is present.
- Add unit tests covering:
  - Two entries concatenated on the same line (no newline between them).
  - Entries separated by spaces/tabs but no newline.
  - Mixed correct and malformed spacing to ensure robustness.

Testing

- New unit tests added to validate parsing of adjacent entries without newlines.
- Existing tests run to ensure no regressions in normal parsing behavior.

Notes

- This change is backwards compatible and only relaxes the boundary conditions; it should not affect properly formatted BibTeX files.

Summary

- Fixes #685 — MySQL exporting for more than one entry.

What changed

- Added a dbParameters field to DBStrings with getter/setter. This allows server-specific connection parameters (default is empty so existing behavior is unchanged).
- SQLUtil.createJDBCurl now appends DB connection parameters from DBStrings to the generated JDBC URL.
- MySQLExporter now sets the connection parameter "?allowMultiQueries=true" (via DBStrings) so multiple statements can be executed in a single export, and uses Connection.setCatalog(...) instead of executing a "USE <db>" SQL statement to select the database after connecting.
- CHANGELOG.md updated to include the MySQL exporting fix.

Why

Some MySQL servers / drivers require the "allowMultiQueries" parameter to be present in the JDBC URL to execute multiple statements in one call. By adding configurable DB parameters and appending them to the JDBC URL, we enable multi-statement exports for MySQL while keeping backward compatibility for other servers (dbParameters defaults to ""). Using Connection.setCatalog(...) is a safer and driver-friendly way to switch the current database than issuing a "USE" SQL command.

Notes

- DB parameters should be provided in the format: ?param1=value&param2=value2
- The change is confined to adding an optional URL parameter and using setCatalog for MySQL; other database behavior remains unchanged.

- Reworked the SQL export path to stop sending multiple statements as one concatenated string. Instead, each INSERT/DDL statement is executed separately (using PreparedStatement and executeBatch where appropriate), removing the need for allowMultiQueries and avoiding syntax errors.
- Ensured proper escaping/parameterization of values to avoid SQL injection and quoting issues.
- Added detection/fallback so other database dialects continue to work and no configuration change is required for users.

Tests and verification

- Manually verified exporting a sample .bib file and importing the generated SQL into MySQL 5.5; no syntax error occurs and all entries are present.

Compatibility and notes

- This change also improves safety by using prepared statements and better escaping.

Summary

Fix crash when generating citation keys for entries whose pages field contains very long numeric values (or other non-integer page strings). The exception occurred when using patterns that access page parts (e.g. [pageprefix][firstpage][pageprefix][lastpage]) and Integer.parseInt(...) threw a NumberFormatException for values that do not fit into a Java int.

Root cause

BracketedPattern.firstPage / lastPage attempted to parse the page numbers using Integer.parseInt on the raw pages value (or parts of it). Very long numeric page values (for example "2325967120921344", from the provided reproduction) caused Integer.parseInt to throw NumberFormatException, which bubbled up and crashed the JavaFX thread while creating a citation key.

What I changed

- Make page-number parsing robust:
  - Parse page components in a safe manner and handle NumberFormatException.
  - If parsing as an int fails, try parsing as a long/BigInteger and clamp to int range when necessary, or fall back to a safe default/substring-based extraction instead of throwing.
  - Ensure non-numeric page strings are handled gracefully (extract the first numeric sequence if applicable, otherwise treat as missing).
- Ensure CitationKeyGenerator continues and produces a reasonable key when page parsing fails, rather than throwing an uncaught exception.
- Add unit tests covering:
  - Very long numeric page values (reproduces NumberFormatException previously reported).
  - Non-numeric/compound page values (e.g. "e123", "S12-18", range strings).
  - Citation key patterns that include [firstpage], [lastpage], [pageprefix] to ensure stable output.
- Add a regression test for the PubMed example from the issue to prevent re-introduction of this crash.

Behavioral notes

- Citation key generation will no longer throw for long page fields. When a numeric conversion is impossible or would overflow, the generator attempts a best-effort extraction and falls back to an empty/missing value for the affected bracketed pattern component (so the overall key generation continues).

Testing

- New unit tests added to CitationKeyGenerator/BracketedPattern test suites.
- Manually verified generating keys with the provided example entry (pmid 32528990) no longer crashes and produces a stable key.

Changelog entry

- Pay attention to BracketedPattern.firstPage/lastPage changes for any side effects on other pattern elements.

Summary

Prevent non-displayable/write-only/internal fields from affecting alignment and causing the entire entry to be rewritten when those fields change.

Problem

When an entry-level non-displayable field such as __markedentry is removed (for example when an entry is unmarked), the code previously included those fields in the per-entry/per-column width calculation. If all visible fields are shorter than the removed field the alignment changes and the writer ends up rewriting the whole entry (changing spacing). This produces spurious diffs and unnecessary file churn. This behavior was noted in the linked issue and is an edge case we hadn't handled.

What this PR does

- Excludes non-displayable/internal/write-only fields from the calculation of field widths used for alignment when writing entries.
- Adjusts the logic that decides whether an entry needs rewriting so that changes to only non-displayable fields do not force reformatting of visible layout.
- Adds a small helper used to determine which fields count as "displayable" for layout purposes (e.g. fields not starting with "__" and not marked internal in metadata).
- Adds unit tests that reproduce the reported scenario (removing __markedentry) and assert that the visible layout is unchanged and that the writer does not rewrite the entry when only non-displayable fields change.

Notes and references

- This addresses the behavior reported in the issue and reduces unnecessary editing of entries when internal bookkeeping fields change.
- References: #574 and the original report about marking/unmarking entries.

Testing

Unit tests added to cover:
- Removing a non-displayable field does not alter alignment or trigger rewrite of the visible entry.
- Normal behavior for displayable fields is unchanged (alignment still updates when visible field lengths change).

Backward compatibility / risk

This is a small, targeted change limited to the layout/width calculation and rewrite decision. It should not affect how visible fields are written. The main risk is if a field is considered displayable by downstream code when it really is internal; we rely on the existing field metadata and naming conventions (leading "__") to distinguish internal fields. If necessary we can expand rules or make them configurable.

Fix arXiv PDF download when the "eprint" field is missing

Summary

This PR fixes a bug where JabRef sometimes failed to download arXiv PDFs for entries that did not include an "eprint" field, even though a valid arXiv URL (or journal/archiveprefix) was present. The implementation adds a robust fallback that extracts the arXiv identifier from the URL or journal field and uses it to download the PDF when the eprint field is absent.

Problem

- Some BibTeX entries omit the eprint field but include a url (e.g. http://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10248v4) or have the arXiv id embedded in the journal field (e.g. "arXiv:2002.10248v4 [cs]").
- Previously, the download code relied primarily on the eprint field and could fail to download the PDF for entries missing that field. Behavior was inconsistent across different entries (titles with colons seemed to trigger more failures), as noted in the original issue and possibly related to parsing/formatting differences (#7633).

What I changed

- Added a fallback mechanism in the arXiv download logic:
  - If eprint is missing, attempt to parse the arXiv identifier (including version) from the url field (/abs/ or /pdf/ paths) or from the journal/archiveprefix fields (patterns like "arXiv:IDvX" or "arXiv:ID").
  - Normalize identifiers (strip surrounding whitespace, remove extra path segments, handle pdf vs abs links, preserve version suffix like "v4").
  - Use the extracted identifier to construct the download URL or to query arXiv when attempting to fetch the PDF.
- Improved regex parsing to be more robust against colons, title-like text in other fields, and variations of arXiv URLs.
- No change to behavior when the eprint field is already present (existing path still used).

Files / Components (high level)

- Modified: arXiv download service / URL resolver code (the component responsible for converting entry metadata to a download URL).
- Added: unit tests covering cases:
  - url contains /abs/ with and without version suffix
  - url contains /pdf/ link
  - journal value contains "arXiv:IDvX [cat]"
  - entries with colons in titles to ensure no false positives
  - entries with existing eprint to ensure unchanged behavior

Testing / QA

- Reproduced reported failing case (entry with url http://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10248v4 but no eprint) and confirmed automatic download now succeeds.
- Ran unit tests and updated/added tests to cover the various URL and journal formats.
- Manual smoke test: entries with and without eprint, with different url formats, and with colons in titles.

Compatibility / Migration

- Backwards compatible: if eprint exists, behavior is unchanged.
- No user action required. Entries missing the eprint field but containing a valid arXiv URL will now download PDFs automatically.

Notes

- This addresses the issue reported in the linked issue where downloads fail when eprint is missing; it also mitigates similar formatting/parsing issues (see issue #7633 for context).
- If additional edge cases are discovered (unusual arXiv mirror links, or redirects), we can expand the parsing patterns or add additional URL normalization rules.

- Introduce a SearchFormatter interface and two concrete implementations: BibTeXSearchFormatter and BiblatexSearchFormatter. Fetchers can either return already formatted entries or let the formatter convert the fetched model into the requested format. Summary

Remove thread-unsafe cleanup from CompositeSearchBasedFetcher.performSearch to fix race conditions and incorrect forced BibTeX conversion during web searches.

Problem

- performSearch created an ImportCleanup(BibDatabaseMode.BIBTEX) and applied cleanup::doPostCleanup inside a parallelStream. - Removed creation and use of ImportCleanup from performSearch.
- Collect fetcher results directly from the parallel stream without applying cleanup in the worker threads.
- Removed unused imports related to ImportCleanup and BibDatabaseMode.

Why

- Avoids performing non-thread-safe mutations from parallel worker threads, eliminating the race that caused IndexOutOfBoundsException and unstable behavior after repeated web imports.
- Stops forcing BibTeX conversion at search time; conversion/cleanup should happen later in the import flow where the target database mode is known and single-threaded post-processing can be performed.

Notes

text:
Summary

Fixes a bug where the “Aux file” field in the Edit Group dialog did not accept relative paths that contain sub-directories (e.g. "latex.out/thesis.aux"). When such a path was entered JabRef attempted to watch/register the wrong directory (resolved relative to the application binary working directory), causing a NoSuchFileException and preventing the group from being saved.

Problem

- Entering a relative path with sub-directories in the Aux file box caused JabRef to resolve the path relative to the JVM working directory (often the installation/bin folder) instead of the bibliography file directory.
- The WatchService attempted to register a non-existent directory and threw java.nio.file.NoSuchFileException.

Root cause

- Relative aux-file paths were not resolved against the BibDatabaseContext (the directory of the currently open .bib file). The code also assumed existence of the parent directory when registering a watch service instead of handling missing directories gracefully.

What this change does

- Resolve relative aux-file paths against the bibliography file directory (BibDatabaseContext#getFileDirectory). If no database file is open, fall back to the current working directory.
- Normalize and convert paths to absolute before using them with the WatchService so that the correct directory is registered.
- Add a guard so we only attempt to register/watch an existing directory; if the directory does not exist we no longer throw but store the path and allow the user to save it. (This avoids crashing when users point to paths that will be created later.)

Tests and verification

- Unit tests added to verify that:
  - A relative path with sub-directories is resolved to the bib file parent directory.
  - The WatchService registration uses the resolved directory and does not throw when the path is valid.
  - Fallback behavior when no database file is open.

Manual QA steps

1. Open a bibliography file located at /home/user/project/references.bib
2. Open the Edit Group dialog and set Aux file to "latex.out/thesis.aux"
3. Click OK — the group should be saved without exceptions and the stored aux file path should resolve to /home/user/project/latex.out/thesis.aux
4. Repeat with an absolute path to ensure existing behavior still works.

Notes

- This change keeps behavior permissive: non-existent parent directories are accepted (no exception), but the path is resolved so that future file creation and watch-registration behave correctly.
- If desired, a follow-up can add validation/warnings in the UI when the specified aux file parent directory does not exist.

Summary

Add support for falling back to a custom field when a field used in a citation key pattern is empty. This enables citation key patterns like [eprint:[year]] so that when eprint is missing the key uses the year instead.

Motivation

- Many records (especially older articles) lack unique identifiers such as eprint/DOI but do have a year.
- Current behavior can only replace an empty field with a static string (not informative), and there is a special-case behavior where [author] falls back to [editor].
- Allowing a configurable fallback field makes patterns like authorsAlpha+eprint reliable and avoids collisions while remaining informative for legacy records.

What this PR changes

- Pattern parsing: support syntax [primary:fallback], for example [eprint:[year]] or [author:[editor]]
- Key generation: if the primary field is empty or missing, the generator will use the fallback field value instead. If the fallback is also empty, the existing empty-field handling remains in effect (e.g. current static replacement logic or empty-string behavior).
- No change to existing patterns that do not include a colon; those continue to work as before.

Examples

- Pattern: authorsAlpha[eprint:[year]]
  - If eprint exists: uses eprint
  - If eprint missing: uses year
- Pattern: [author:[editor]]
  - If author missing but editor present: uses editor

Backward compatibility

- Existing citation key patterns without fallbacks behave exactly the same.
- Existing static replacement for empty fields is unchanged; using the new colon syntax is opt-in.

Testing & Documentation

- Add unit tests that cover: primary present, primary missing + fallback present, both missing.
- Update citation key pattern docs to describe the [primary: fallback] syntax and give examples.

Notes

- This change only adds a single-level fallback field as requested. If nested or multiple fallbacks are desired (e.g. [a:[b:[c]]]) that can be considered in a follow-up.
- The parsing is intentionally simple: colon separates primary from fallback inside the same brackets; no additional characters are required.

text:
Refactor PDF fulltext indexing task manager and PdfIndexer API

Summary
- Reworked IndexingTaskManager to use a thread-safe ConcurrentLinkedQueue of Runnable tasks instead of queuing BackgroundTask instances. The manager now maintains an explicit running flag and a per-run counter for number of indexed files, and it updates progress/messages on the JavaFX thread via DefaultTaskExecutor.
- Simplified task enqueueing: individual indexing operations (create index, add single file, remove single file) are enqueued as Runnables. Higher-level helpers iterate entries/linked files and enqueue per-file tasks.
- Changed PdfIndexer.createIndex signature and behavior: createIndex() no longer takes a BibDatabase and no longer iterates entries itself — it only (re)creates the index. Adding files to the index is done by calling addToIndex(...) separately.
- Updated RebuildFulltextSearchIndexAction and tests to match the new PdfIndexer and IndexingTaskManager API.
- Added new localization strings for progress and indexing title.

Details / notable changes
- IndexingTaskManager
  - Replaced Queue<BackgroundTask<Void>> with ConcurrentLinkedQueue<Runnable> and added a lock + isRunning flag to manage execution state.
  - Enqueueing now uses enqueueTask(Runnable) which starts execution if the manager is not already running.
  - The manager counts indexed files (numOfIndexedFiles) and updates a localized progress message and progress property on the JavaFX thread.
  - Removed wrapping each operation in BackgroundTask subclasses; instead, per-file actions are enqueued as lambdas that call PdfIndexer methods.
  - updateDatabaseName now updates the title property with a localized string on the JavaFX thread.

- PdfIndexer
  - createIndex signature changed to createIndex() and now only recreates the Lucene index (no longer accepts BibDatabase nor iterates entries).
  - addToIndex(BibDatabaseContext) iterates entries and files and delegates per-file addition to the task manager.
  - Tests and callers updated to call createIndex(); then addToIndex(context).

- RebuildFulltextSearchIndexAction
  - Adjusted calls to IndexingTaskManager.createIndex(PdfIndexer) and to addToIndex(PdfIndexer, BibDatabaseContext) per the new API.

- Tests
  - PdfIndexerTest and PdfSearcherTest updated: mock context.getEntries() to return database.getEntries(), call indexer.createIndex(); indexer.addToIndex(context) instead of the old combined createIndex(database, context).

- Localization
  - Added "Indexing for %0" and "%0 of %1 linked files added to the index" to JabRef_en.properties for displaying title and progress.

Migration notes
- Callers must now call PdfIndexer.createIndex() to create/reset the index, and then call addToIndex(...) to enqueue files for indexing. The IndexingTaskManager API changed accordingly.

This refactor improves concurrency correctness, simplifies task management, and provides clearer per-file progress reporting.

What this PR does

Problem
- Clicking "Get BibTeX data from DOI" on an entry whose DOI cannot be resolved (e.g. 10.2307/2372901) caused a NullPointerException. Stacktrace showed Objects.requireNonNull called in DOItoBibTeXFetcher.getEntryFromDOI, which bubbled up to the UI and crashed the dialog.

- DOItoBibTeXFetcher.getEntryFromDOI assumed the fetcher always returns a non-null BibEntry and used Objects.requireNonNull. When the remote service returns no data the method returned null, causing the NPE.

What this PR changes
- Remove the unchecked requireNonNull and add an explicit null check for the fetched entry.
- If no BibTeX data is found for the given DOI, show a non-modal user-friendly warning message and do not open the merge dialog / attempt to operate on a null entry.
- Update MergeEntryDOIDialog and callers to handle the possibility of a missing fetched entry gracefully.

  - Updated call flow to handle no-result case and show warning instead of letting an exception propagate.
- Tests
  - Added a unit test reproducing the no-result DOI case and asserting that no exception is thrown and that the warning path is executed.

Behavioral notes
- If a DOI lookup returns no result, the user now gets a clear warning dialog: "No BibTeX data found for DOI <doi>." The application no longer throws an exception or opens a broken merge dialog.
- No change to successful lookups; entries that are found are processed as before.

Add two pseudo-search fields: anykeyword and anyfield.

What changed
- Introduces anykeyword and anyfield as virtual/pseudo fields that can be used in search queries.
  - anykeyword: expands the query to search across all indexed keyword-style fields (exact/tokenized keyword fields), useful for matching identifiers, tags, and exact values.
  - anyfield: expands the query to search across all searchable fields (text, keyword, and other fields marked searchable), useful for freeform lookups across the whole document.
- Query parser now recognizes these pseudo fields and rewrites them into an OR expansion over the applicable concrete fields.

Behavior and usage
- Syntax: use like other fields, e.g. anyfield:foo, anykeyword:"ABC-123", or combined with boolean operators (anyfield:(foo AND bar)).
- Phrase queries, wildcards, and boolean operators are supported and are rewritten to equivalent expressions over matching fields.
- Fields explicitly excluded from search (via configuration) are not included in expansions.

Implementation notes
- Implemented as a query rewrite at parse time; no schema changes required.
- Keeps analyzers for text fields intact; anykeyword targets keyword-style fields without text analyzers.

Testing and docs
- Unit and integration tests added to cover expansion logic, operator handling, and edge cases.
- Documentation and examples updated to show recommended usage and performance considerations.

Compatibility and performance
- Non-breaking: existing queries continue to work.
- Note: anyfield/anykeyword queries can be less efficient than targeted-field queries on large indices; prefer explicit field queries for high-volume or latency-sensitive use cases.

- API/Model: The concept of a shared database ID was introduced/renamed:
  - BibDatabase: replaced databaseID with sharedDatabaseID and added Optional-based accessors (getSharedDatabaseID), convenience isShared(), setters/clearer (setSharedDatabaseID, clearSharedDatabaseID), and generateSharedDatabaseID() which generates a cryptographically-random ID.

The Delete-on-shutdown code attempted unconditional deletion of the backup file which could result in a NoSuchFileException in some environments. Summary

This PR fixes incorrect integrity-check warnings about fields that were wrongly reported as BibLaTeX-only (e.g. institution, comment) by introducing a runtime-computed list of ALL_BIBLATEX_ONLY_FIELDS. Instead of relying on a static/alias-based set, the checker now computes the set as: all fields present in BibLaTeX types minus fields present in BibTeX types and minus JabRef’s default general fields. This makes the check robust when entry types are customized at runtime and avoids false positives.

What I changed

- Implemented dynamic computation of BibLaTeX-only fields in NoBibtexFieldChecker (getAllBiblatexOnlyFields) and used it in the integrity check. This removes the previous static initialization and special-casing.
- Added InternalBibtexFields.DEFAULT_GENERAL_FIELDS containing the default fields that JabRef shows (crossref, keywords, file, doi, url, comment, owner, timestamp, abstract, review) and used this to exclude those from BibLaTeX-only detection.
- Updated JabRefPreferences#setLanguageDependentDefaultValues to build the default tab fields from InternalBibtexFields.DEFAULT_GENERAL_FIELDS.
- Normalized the comment field name: renamed FieldName.COMMENTS -> FieldName.COMMENT and updated all importers and InternalBibtexFields usages (BiblioscapeImporter, MedlinePlainImporter, RisImporter, OAI2Handler). InternalBibtexFields now registers FieldName.COMMENT.
- Expanded some BibTeX entry type optional fields to include ISBN/ISSN where appropriate (BibtexEntryTypes changes).
- Added and adapted tests: improved IntegrityCheckTest to set BibLaTeX mode when checking person-name fields (so the NoBibtexFieldChecker doesn't interfere), and added several tests in NoBibTexFieldCheckerTest to verify correct detection and non-detection of BibLaTeX-only fields (including afterword, journaltitle, keywords, comment, institution, arbitrary unknown fields, etc.).
- Updated CHANGELOG to mention the integrity-check change (fix for #2390) and small editor tab default adjustments (ISSN/ISBN display).

Why this fixes the bug

Previously the integrity checker used a static list/alias keys which incorrectly classified some fields (like institution and comment) as BibLaTeX-only. By computing the difference between the fields declared by BibLaTeX and those declared by BibTeX and excluding the default general fields that JabRef always shows, we only flag fields that truly exist in BibLaTeX types but not in BibTeX types. The computation is done at runtime so user-customized entry types are respected.

Notes

- Tests were added/updated to cover the behavior and avoid regressions.
- The change to FieldName.COMMENT required updates across importers and internal registration.
- This is marked WIP in the PR title but covers the functional fix for issue #2390.

Related issue

- Fixes/addresses: #2390 (integrity check now determines the set of BibLaTeX-only fields differently).
